advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the wire-byte measurement with FastMCP emitting both a content text block and structuredContent — the true transport payload is ~2x the measured structuredContent.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_budget.py:130 `return _payload_bytes({"result": js_safe_result(list(rows))})` measures a single serialization
src/rebar/_mcp_budget.py:124-126 docstring claims it measures 'the exact object FastMCP serializes into structuredContent'

src/rebar/_mcp_errors.py:181 'FastMCP derives BOTH the ``content`` text block and ``structuredContent`` from the SAME returned object' — the transport frame carries both, so the on-wire size is ~2x the structuredContent alone
The change's stated invariant is that under-estimating 'passes a payload that still overruns' (_mcp_budget.py:111-112); measuring one of two emitted copies re-introduces a ~2x under-estimate
advisory.finding: `_wire_bytes` measures only the `{"result": ...}` object serialized once (the structuredContent), but FastMCP emits BOTH a `content` text block and `structuredContent` derived from that same object, so the bytes the client actually receives are roughly double the measured value — the bound still under-reports the real wire payload, the direction the docstring explicitly calls the dangerous one.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either account for the duplicated content block (e.g. measure/estimate both blocks) or document explicitly that the budget measures the structuredContent block only and lower the numeric budget to leave headroom for the mirrored content block.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the convergence-twin `wire_measure == actual` assertion with one that measures the object FastMCP actually serializes (e.g. drive a real _call and compare its structuredContent bytes) rather than re-running _wire_bytes's own pipeline.
evidence: Test: `wire_measure = _wire_bytes(models)` then `actual = len(json.dumps({"result": js_safe_result(models)}, default=str))` then `assert wire_measure == actual`
The two sides differ only by `list(rows)` vs `models`, an identical construction — same logic re-derived, not an independent oracle.
advisory.finding: In test_budget_is_measured_on_the_wire_payload_not_the_raw_reducer_rows, the assertion `wire_measure == actual` is a convergence twin: `_wire_bytes(models)` computes `_payload_bytes({"result": js_safe_result(list(rows))})` and `actual` is computed as `len(json.dumps({"result": js_safe_result(models)}, default=str))` — the identical js_safe_result + json.dumps pipeline. The equality therefore verifies the function returns what its own body computes, not that it measures the object FastMCP actually serializes into structuredContent; it would stay green if _wire_bytes measured the wrong shape as long as `actual` mirrored the same mistake.
